Multivariate count regression

Source: R/countreg_mv.R
countreg_mv.Rd

Fits several count outcomes observed on the same units, such as crashes by severity or by type at each site, each with its own count family, mean formula and distribution-parameter formulas.

Usage

countreg_mv(
  formula,
  data,
  family = "NB2",
  dis_param_formula_1 = NULL,
  dis_param_formula_2 = NULL,
  offset = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  group_var = NULL,
  stderr = "normal",
  method = "BFGS",
  max.iters = 1000,
  start.vals = NULL,
  ndraws = 1500,
  engine = "quadrature",
  verbose = FALSE,
  .setup_only = FALSE
)

Arguments

formula

either a formula with the outcomes on the left as cbind(y_1, ..., y_J) and one right-hand side for every equation, or a list of two-sided formulas, one per outcome (named by the list names, or by their responses). An offset() term (an exposure) belongs in the formulas.

data

a data frame.

family

the count family of each outcome (see count_families): one code for every outcome, or one per outcome (named by outcome or in their order). Families made with new_count_family() are accepted.

dis_param_formula_1, dis_param_formula_2

formulas for the outcomes' distribution parameters, as in countreg(): NULL (constant), one one-sided formula for every outcome that has the parameter, or a list named by outcome (outcomes not in the list keep a constant parameter).

offset

optional names of offset columns (log scale) used by every equation, instead of offset() in the formulas.

weights

optional frequency weights: a column name or a numeric vector.

group_var

optional column naming the units for cluster-robust standard errors (such as a site observed over several years).

stderr

"normal" (from the Hessian, the default), "robust" (sandwich) or "cluster" (sandwich by group_var).

method, max.iters, start.vals, verbose

optimizer settings, as in countreg(); the default method is "BFGS".

ndraws, engine

integration settings of families without a closed form, as in countreg().

.setup_only

internal use: return the model setup without fitting.

Value

An object of class "countreg_mv", with methods coef(), vcov(), logLik(), summary(), predict(), fitted(), residuals(), simulate(), tidy(), glance() and confint().

Details

Independent equations. The outcomes are independent given the covariates, so the log-likelihood is the sum of the equations' log-likelihoods and every equation's estimates equal those of a separate countreg() fit. Fitting them together gives one object with joint predictions, simulations and tests across equations (for example, a Wald test that a coefficient is the same in two equations). The rows used are those complete for every equation.

Different outcomes often need different families: frequent property damage crashes may be close to NB2, while rare fatal crashes are more skewed and zero-heavy. Each equation can use any family of the package.

See also

predict.countreg_mv(), countreg(), countreg_alloc() for a total and its split across categories, negmultinom()

Examples

# \donttest{
data("washington_roads")
w <- washington_roads
w$pdo <- w$Total_crashes - w$Injury_crashes
m <- countreg_mv(cbind(pdo, Injury_crashes) ~ lnaadt + speed50 +
                   offset(lnlength), data = w,
                 family = c(pdo = "NB2", Injury_crashes = "PIG"))
summary(m)
#> Multivariate count model

#> Std. errors: normal

#>

#>

head(predict(m))
